abiEvidence.identityLimit: Verified source/ABI/deployment metadata and service proxy resolution are inventory evidence, not fresh proof of runtime identity. No alternative generic vault/fork ABI was substituted.

Approval(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when the allowance of a `spender` for an `owner` is set by a call to {approve}. `value` is the new allowance.

RoleAdminChanged(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32.details: Emitted when `newAdminRole` is set as ``role``'s admin role, replacing `previousAdminRole` `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is the starting admin for all roles, despite {RoleAdminChanged} not being emitted signaling this. _Available since v3.1._

RoleGranted(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is granted `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call, an admin role bearer except when using {AccessControl-_setupRole}.

RoleRevoked(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)

Transfer(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to another (`to`). Note that `value` may be zero.

params._allocBPS: The strategy allocation in basis points
params._feeBPS: The performance fee (taken from profit) in basis points

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `amount` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

balance().details: It calculates the total underlying value of {token} held by the system. It takes into account the vault contract idle funds, and the capital deployed across all the strategies.

decimals().details: Overrides the default 18 decimals for the vault ERC20 to match the same decimals as the underlying token used

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

params._amount: The amount of assets to deposit

depositAll().details: A helper function to call deposit() with all the sender's funds.

getPricePerFullShare().details: Function for various UIs to display the current value of one of our yield tokens. Returns an uint256 with 18 decimals of how much underlying asset one vault share represents.

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

getRoleMember(bytes32,uint256).details: Returns one of the accounts that have `role`. `index` must be a value between 0 and {getRoleMemberCount}, non-inclusive. Role bearers are not sorted in any particular way, and their ordering may change at any point. WARNING: When using {getRoleMember} and {getRoleMemberCount}, make sure you perform all queries on the same block. See the following https://forum.openzeppelin.com/t/iterating-over-elements-on-enumerableset-in-openzeppelin-contracts/2296[forum post] for more information.

getRoleMemberCount(bytes32).details: Returns the number of accounts that have `role`. Can be used together with {getRoleMember} to enumerate all bearers of a role.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

inCaseTokensGetStuck(address).details: Rescues random funds stuck that the strat can't handle.

params._token: address of the token to rescue.

increaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically increases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

injectTokens(uint256).details: Super-Admin function to inject tokens directly into the vault      without going through the deposit flow. Used in tests to verify      ERC4626 share price behavior.

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

removeTvlCap().details: helper function to remove TVL cap

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

params._repayment: The repayment of debt by the strategy.
params._roi: The return on investment (positive or negative) given as the total amount gained or lost from the harvest.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

params.degradation: - The rate of degradation in percent per second scaled to 1e18.

params._withdrawalQueue: The new withdrawalQueue to update to.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `amount`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. This is not required by the EIP. See the note at the beginning of {ERC20}. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `amount`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `amount`.

params._allocBPS: The strategy allocation in basis points

params._feeBPS: The new performance fee in basis points.

updateTvlCap(uint256).details: pass in max value of uint to effectively remove TVL cap.

params._withdrawMaxLoss: The new value, in basis points.

params._shares: the number of shares to burn

withdrawAll().details: A helper function to call withdraw() with all the sender's funds.

STRATEGIST().notice: Reaper Roles in increasing order of privilege. {STRATEGIST} - Role conferred to authors of the strategy, allows for tweaking non-critical params. {GUARDIAN} - Multisig requiring 2 signatures for invoking emergency measures. {ADMIN}- Multisig requiring 3 signatures for deactivating emergency measures and changing TVL cap. The DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (in-built access control role) will be granted to a multisig requiring 4 signatures. This role would have the ability to add strategies, as well as the ability to grant any other roles. Also note that roles are cascading. So any higher privileged role should be able to perform all the functions of any lower privileged role.

addStrategy(address,uint256,uint256).notice: Adds a new strategy to the vault with a given allocation amount in basis points.

availableCapital().notice: Called by a strategy to determine the amount of capital that the vault is able to provide it. A positive amount means that vault has excess capital to provide the strategy, while a negative amount means that the strategy has a balance owing to the vault.

deposit(uint256).notice: The entrypoint of funds into the system. People deposit with this function into the vault.

report(int256,uint256).notice: Main contact point where each strategy interacts with the vault during its harvest to report profit/loss as well as any repayment of debt.

revokeStrategy(address).notice: Removes any allocation to a given strategy.

setEmergencyShutdown(bool).notice: Activates or deactivates Vault mode where all Strategies go into full withdrawal. During Emergency Shutdown: 1. No Users may deposit into the Vault (but may withdraw as usual.) 2. New Strategies may not be added. 3. Each Strategy must pay back their debt as quickly as reasonable to minimally affect their position. If true, the Vault goes into Emergency Shutdown. If false, the Vault goes back into Normal Operation.

setWithdrawalQueue(address[]).notice: Updates the withdrawalQueue to match the addresses and order specified.

updateStrategyAllocBPS(address,uint256).notice: Updates the allocation points for a given strategy.

updateTreasury(address).notice: Only DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can update treasury address.

updateTvlCap(uint256).notice: Updates the vault tvl cap (the max amount of assets held by the vault).

updateWithdrawMaxLoss(uint256).notice: Updates the withdrawMaxLoss which is the maximum allowed slippage.

withdraw(uint256).notice: Function to exit the system. The vault will withdraw the required tokens from the strategies and pay up the token holder. A proportional number of IOU tokens are burned in the process.

selectedFunctions.label: Reaper Farm Deposit WETH to receiver
warnings: Static source/ABI function inventory only; no current runtime identity, successful execution, funding, backing, liquidity, financial-safety or complete-workflow assurance. Calls require zero native value and remain subject to independent grants, pauses and canonical-calldata controls.

This is the current official frontend’s experimental WETH Alpha Multi-Strategy Vault on Optimism, not inactive standard vaults. The alpha UI says strategies are actively tested/developed, may not work as expected and are used at the user’s own risk. Alpha status is a material restriction, not a production-quality guarantee.

Underlying is 18-decimal WETH 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, not native ETH. Deposits/mint transfer caller WETH using vault allowance; receiver gets transferable vault shares. depositAll spends the caller’s full WETH balance. Deposits require positive amount, no emergencyShutdown and vault capacity; small positive deposits can floor to zero shares.

Share conversion uses free funds after locked profit, not gross strategy balances. Deposit/redeem conversions floor; previewMint/previewWithdraw round up. mint computes rounded-up assets and calls _deposit without checking the number of shares minted. No caller-set min shares, min assets, max input or deadline exists.

Legacy withdraw(uint256)/withdrawAll use caller shares and can burn fewer shares/pay less if the configured withdrawal queue cannot satisfy all assets. Strategy-reported losses reduce payout and are checked against operator-set withdrawMaxLoss. ERC4626 withdraw requires returned assets exactly equal requested assets; redeem requires exactly the requested owner shares burned, otherwise the whole call reverts. These stronger checks do not make payouts lossless.

ERC4626 withdraw/redeem can act for owner using existing owner-to-caller vault-share allowance; self-withdrawal needs no share allowance. Receiver is explicit only in ERC4626 variants; legacy withdrawals pay caller. No arbitrary target, route, zap, strategy maintenance or harvest surface is admitted.

Official current alpha configuration labels Sonne and Yearn substrategies, but this is not a current allocation/strategy-identity attestation. Operator-configured strategies/queue, fees, locked-profit degradation, loss tolerance and token dependencies can change or revert calls. UI advertises 10% interest fee and zero deposit/withdraw fee; source uses per-strategy performance fees and strategy losses rather than a guaranteed fixed net return.

Explorer rendering observed emergencyShutdown=false, WETH underlying, uncapped uint256-max tvlCap and withdrawMaxLoss=1 basis point. Values are point-in-time explorer evidence, not persistent state. No strategy cash, asset availability, approval, investment eligibility or execution guarantee is implied. Reviewed vault entry methods have no explicit KYC allowlist gate; independent legal and frontend restrictions still apply.

This is the current official frontend’s experimental WETH Alpha Multi-Strategy Vault on Optimism, not inactive standard vaults. The alpha UI says strategies are actively tested/developed, may not work as expected and are used at the user’s own risk. Alpha status is a material restriction, not a production-quality guarantee.

Underlying is 18-decimal WETH 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, not native ETH. Deposits/mint transfer caller WETH using vault allowance; receiver gets transferable vault shares. depositAll spends the caller’s full WETH balance. Deposits require positive amount, no emergencyShutdown and vault capacity; small positive deposits can floor to zero shares.

Share conversion uses free funds after locked profit, not gross strategy balances. Deposit/redeem conversions floor; previewMint/previewWithdraw round up. mint computes rounded-up assets and calls _deposit without checking the number of shares minted. No caller-set min shares, min assets, max input or deadline exists.

Legacy withdraw(uint256)/withdrawAll use caller shares and can burn fewer shares/pay less if the configured withdrawal queue cannot satisfy all assets. Strategy-reported losses reduce payout and are checked against operator-set withdrawMaxLoss. ERC4626 withdraw requires returned assets exactly equal requested assets; redeem requires exactly the requested owner shares burned, otherwise the whole call reverts. These stronger checks do not make payouts lossless.

ERC4626 withdraw/redeem can act for owner using existing owner-to-caller vault-share allowance; self-withdrawal needs no share allowance. Receiver is explicit only in ERC4626 variants; legacy withdrawals pay caller. No arbitrary target, route, zap, strategy maintenance or harvest surface is admitted.

Official current alpha configuration labels Sonne and Yearn substrategies, but this is not a current allocation/strategy-identity attestation. Operator-configured strategies/queue, fees, locked-profit degradation, loss tolerance and token dependencies can change or revert calls. UI advertises 10% interest fee and zero deposit/withdraw fee; source uses per-strategy performance fees and strategy losses rather than a guaranteed fixed net return.

Explorer rendering observed emergencyShutdown=false, WETH underlying, uncapped uint256-max tvlCap and withdrawMaxLoss=1 basis point. Values are point-in-time explorer evidence, not persistent state. No strategy cash, asset availability, approval, investment eligibility or execution guarantee is implied. Reviewed vault entry methods have no explicit KYC allowlist gate; independent legal and frontend restrictions still apply.

sourceSemantics.assetAndApprovals: 18-decimal WETH; _deposit uses token.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender,this,amount), mints floor-converted shares to receiver and records idle capital. Whole-balance depositAll reads caller WETH. No native wrapping/unwrapping or prefunding step.
sourceSemantics.entryGates: _deposit requires !emergencyShutdown, amount !=0 and balance()+amount<=tvlCap; it does not require positive shares after flooring. No explicit KYC/caller allowlist in selected vault entry/exit functions.
sourceSemantics.roundingAndProfit: _freeFunds equals balance minus gradually unlocked profit. Deposits and _withdraw value floor. previewMint/previewWithdraw round up; mint ignores the _deposit return value and does not explicitly assert exact requested shares.
sourceSemantics.exitOwnership: Legacy withdraw/withdrawAll burn caller shares and pay caller. ERC4626 overloads use explicit receiver/owner, spending existing owner share allowance only if owner != caller.
sourceSemantics.liquidityAndLoss: _withdraw traverses configured strategy withdrawalQueue only if idle assets are insufficient. Strategy loss reduces payout; if cash remains short it reduces burned shares and caps assets to available idle. totalLoss is bounded by current withdrawMaxLoss BPS. This is synchronous strategy queue traversal, not an asynchronous user withdrawal request/claim queue.
sourceSemantics.erc4626ExitChecks: withdraw(assets,receiver,owner) computes ceil shares then requires _withdraw result == assets; redeem(shares,receiver,owner) requires exactly shares burned. If either equality fails all effects revert.
sourceSemantics.feesAndControl: No direct deposit/exit fee is charged in _deposit/_withdraw, but mutable strategy performance-fee reporting and withdrawal losses affect value. Alpha frontend displays 10% interest fee; source/current configuration are not fixed-fee or net-return guarantees. Roles can change cap, loss tolerance, profit locking, strategies, queue and treasury.
sourceSemantics.experimentalAndDependencies: Current frontend names this alpha vault, not inactive standard WETH vaults. Its explicit alpha disclaimer says active development/testing and may not work as expected. Sonne/Yearn strategy labels are frontend configuration only, not current deployed strategy allocations/source identity. These configured dependencies are not callable catalog capabilities and may revert. No arbitrary zap, executor or callback surface is selected.
sourceSemantics.timingAndRecipients: No selected function has caller deadline/minimum-out/maximum-in parameters. No fixed withdrawal delay is implemented; output depends on current free funds/strategy cash/losses. No execution readiness or legal suitability is asserted.

lifecycleEvidence.excerpt: # Inactive Vaults Sometimes protocols make changes to their own technology and require migration of funds to new pools. Sometimes protocols shut down entirely. Whatever the case, Reaper will never touch your assets or move funds on your behalf, beyond the automated internal contracts of vaults. If a strategy is no longer supported, the vault will be marked inactive. This means that users will not be able to deposit funds into said vaults, however this does not affect your ability to withdraw your funds. You will always be able to withdraw your funds from inactive vaults. ## Can't find a vault? Inactive vaults may be removed from the front end. If that is the case, funds remain safe and withdrawals can still be processed via the smart contract. To do so, search for your wallet address in FTMScan (). Find your vault shares in the Token Holdings dropdown. The token should have a name starting with "rf". Click on it to head to the vault contract. Scroll down and select Contract, then Write Contract, as pictured: Find the function named "withdrawAll", click the dropdown, and Write. This will cost some gas but will withdraw all of your LPs from the vault. You can then go to the relevant DEX and stake or split your LPs as you wish!
lifecycleEvidence.interpretation: Official inactive-vault policy says unsupported strategies are marked inactive and deposits disabled; no exit-only exception is used here.

limitations: Static source/ABI function inventory only; no current runtime identity, successful execution, funding, backing, liquidity, financial-safety or complete-workflow assurance. Calls require zero native value and remain subject to independent grants, pauses and canonical-calldata controls.

This is the current official frontend’s experimental WETH Alpha Multi-Strategy Vault on Optimism, not inactive standard vaults. The alpha UI says strategies are actively tested/developed, may not work as expected and are used at the user’s own risk. Alpha status is a material restriction, not a production-quality guarantee.

Underlying is 18-decimal WETH 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, not native ETH. Deposits/mint transfer caller WETH using vault allowance; receiver gets transferable vault shares. depositAll spends the caller’s full WETH balance. Deposits require positive amount, no emergencyShutdown and vault capacity; small positive deposits can floor to zero shares.

Share conversion uses free funds after locked profit, not gross strategy balances. Deposit/redeem conversions floor; previewMint/previewWithdraw round up. mint computes rounded-up assets and calls _deposit without checking the number of shares minted. No caller-set min shares, min assets, max input or deadline exists.

Legacy withdraw(uint256)/withdrawAll use caller shares and can burn fewer shares/pay less if the configured withdrawal queue cannot satisfy all assets. Strategy-reported losses reduce payout and are checked against operator-set withdrawMaxLoss. ERC4626 withdraw requires returned assets exactly equal requested assets; redeem requires exactly the requested owner shares burned, otherwise the whole call reverts. These stronger checks do not make payouts lossless.

ERC4626 withdraw/redeem can act for owner using existing owner-to-caller vault-share allowance; self-withdrawal needs no share allowance. Receiver is explicit only in ERC4626 variants; legacy withdrawals pay caller. No arbitrary target, route, zap, strategy maintenance or harvest surface is admitted.

Official current alpha configuration labels Sonne and Yearn substrategies, but this is not a current allocation/strategy-identity attestation. Operator-configured strategies/queue, fees, locked-profit degradation, loss tolerance and token dependencies can change or revert calls. UI advertises 10% interest fee and zero deposit/withdraw fee; source uses per-strategy performance fees and strategy losses rather than a guaranteed fixed net return.

Explorer rendering observed emergencyShutdown=false, WETH underlying, uncapped uint256-max tvlCap and withdrawMaxLoss=1 basis point. Values are point-in-time explorer evidence, not persistent state. No strategy cash, asset availability, approval, investment eligibility or execution guarantee is implied. Reviewed vault entry methods have no explicit KYC allowlist gate; independent legal and frontend restrictions still apply.
